query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small boron micro-alloying addition (≈2 at.% B substituted for the transition-metal content) into a phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy (HEA) will simultaneously (a) raise the reduced glass-transition temperature Trg (= Tg/Tl) by ≥0.03 and (b) increase the onset crystallisation temperature Tx by ≥20 K, compared with the same alloy lacking boron, when both are processed under identical rapid-quenching conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted, melt-spun ribbon or suction-cast rod of a multicomponent (≥5 principal elements) transition-metal HEA containing 3–12 at.% P but no intentional boron.
generation.intervention: Replace ~2 at.% of the metallic content with elemental boron, keeping total metalloid (P + B) content below 15 at.% and re-melt under identical processing parameters.
generation.conditions: Quench rates ≥105 K s⁻¹; overall composition still inside the known amorphous-forming domain (negative average mixing enthalpy, atomic-size mismatch >6 %). Effect expected for B additions ≤4 at.%; above this, early boride precipitation or liquid immiscibility may nullify the benefit.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of additional three-member (B–P–M) covalent clusters that deepen the metastable eutectic and increase chemical/size frustration, promoting dense random packing and suppressing diffusion-controlled rearrangements.
generation.mechanism: Boron’s small atomic radius and strong negative mixing enthalpy with both P and early transition metals create locally favoured structures that (i) lower the liquidus temperature Tl, boosting Trg, and (ii) raise the energy barrier for cooperative atomic rearrangement, delaying the first crystallisation event (higher Tx).
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with the B-free baseline, the 2 at.% B alloy will show (1) an increase in critical casting thickness dc by at least 50 % or absolute 0.5 mm (whichever is larger) and (2) a DSC-measured increase of Tx–Tg by ≥20 K, indicating improved thermal stability of the amorphous phase.
generation.baseline: Same nominal multi-principal alloy composition but containing no intentional boron; processed under identical melting and quenching conditions.
generation.boundary: If the alloy already contains >15 at.% cumulative metalloids, or if B content exceeds ~4 at.% leading to primary boride formation, the intervention will not improve—and may degrade—GFA and Tx.
generation.uncertainty: Evidence for B-induced GFA improvement is strong in binary and ternary metallic glasses, but direct data for P-bearing HEAs are sparse; magnitude of Tx shift (≥20 K) is therefore uncertain to ±10 K.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys: (A) baseline (no B) and (B) B-modified (2 at.% B, overall composition otherwise identical). Produce melt-spun ribbons and 2 mm suction-cast rods from each melt under identical thermal histories. Characterise by DSC and X-ray diffraction.
measurements: Liquidus temperature Tl (from DSC on remelted samples)
Supercooled liquid region ΔTx = Tx – Tg
Critical casting thickness dc (largest fully amorphous rod verified by XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If alloy (B) fails to show BOTH (i) Trg increase of ≥0.03 OR dc increase of ≥50 % over alloy (A) AND (ii) Tx increase of ≥20 K, the hypothesis is falsified.
